originality.rationale: The primary source proves generator-moment sufficiency and presents an unspecified-support rank test, not a complete exponent-dependent rank phase diagram. New proof identifies exactly eta=1,2 as rank-defective for every three-size support and recovers identifiability with two separate natural protocols; its strict-curvature lemma and joint inverse-moment argument go beyond simply asserting the published rank criterion. Other inspected studies concern different network/ODE observation structures. Priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Older inverse-moment or experimental-design literature may independently imply the rank geometry; this literature is too broad for exhaustive historical priority.
The original paper already formulates the generalized rank test, so the contribution is its precise resolution and combined-protocol theorem, not moment equivalence itself.
Theoretical two-protocol observation presumes the same group-size law and calibrated transmission scale across protocols.

value.rationale: The biologically motivated per-partner and prevalence-squared normalizations lead to unexpected exact rank loss, forcing nonidentifiability from complete epidemic rates on just three group sizes. An explicit pair of differently normalized observations restores three-size identification, with sharp minimal-support boundaries. This is a directly usable structural-inference theorem rather than a routine threshold substitution.
